newsitem.title: ROMANIA: End-Sept foreign investment in Romania $2.03 bln.
newsitem.headline: End-Sept foreign investment in Romania $2.03 bln.

text.p: Total direct foreign investment in Romania since the fall of communism in 1989 stood at some $2.03 billion at the end of September, the Romanian Development Agency (ARD) said on Thursday.

The foreign investment level in Romania remains low in comparison with other ex-communist countries in Eastern and Central Europe. Some economists say inadequate corporate laws and red tape are what keep foreign investors to the sidelines.
According to the ARD, the main foreign investment promoter, South Korea's Daewoo Heavy Industries Ltd is the largest single investor in Romania with $212 million pumped into joint ventures here.

Last year, Daewoo bought 51 percent of a local carmaker which it plans to develop further on the strength of $1.0 billion investment by 2000. In May, Daewoo added shipbuilding to its Romanian interests, buying a majority stake in a Black Sea shipyard.
Some analysts say foreign investment in Romania will pick up only if privatisation is accelerated and restructuring of oversized industrial firms gets well under way.

Others believe a selloff of 4,000 companies will encourage foreigners to step into Romania, as will the stock exchange, in operation since last November, and an over-the-counter market expected to start trading later this month.
